A and B both pass all 21 probes and meet all 19 requirements. What separates them is that A ships 15 passing tests and B ships none. B handles one edge case better.

**How they differ:**

| | A | B |
|---|---|---|
| Probes passed | 21 / 21 | 21 / 21 |
| Own tests | 15 passed, 0 failed | none |
| Ruff findings | 20 (style: old-style `%` formatting, a missing exception chain, a complex `main`) | 8 (complex functions, missing exception chains, long lines) |
| Bandit | 2 low, both in its test file's subprocess call | none |
| Lines of code | 284 | 308 |
| Scores (functional / coverage / security / robustness / quality / tests) | 5 / 5 / 5 / 4 / 4 / 5 | 5 / 5 / 5 / 5 / 4 / 0 |

- **A's edge case:** if you add a job whose dependency has already failed, A leaves it `pending` forever, so it can never run. B marks it `cancelled`. I checked this by hand, not with a probe, because the task only says what happens to dependents at the moment a job fails. I rated it low.
- **A's save:** it always writes through the same temporary file name and doesn't lock the state file, so two runs at the same time could overwrite each other. Also low.
- **Neither side has a security issue** beyond those two bandit lows.

**Two things to keep in mind when reading the probes:**
- **Cycle check:** you can't create a cycle with `add` alone, because unknown dependencies are rejected and a new job can't be a dependency yet. So that probe writes a state file that already contains a cycle and checks the program rejects it cleanly.
- **Invocation:** A takes `--depends-on` as space-separated ids and B as comma-separated, so that is the only thing the probes change per side. I ran them with Python 3.11 because the system's 3.9 lacks a feature the stdlib-only check needs.

I couldn't tell which side was built with a spec framework (confidence 0.3). The two programs are structured almost the same way, and A's test suite is only a weak hint.

Files are in the task directory:
- `requirements.json`
- `probes/run_probes.py`
- `probes/results.json`
- `judgment.json`
